description.narrative: The Project is expected to deliver substantial environmental and social benefits by supporting Santander's growth in its sustainable finance portfolio. Specifically, the financing will help the bank fund its commitment under the Brazilian government's Eco Invest program to finance US$1.2 billion in Eco Invest assets. Furthermore, 30% of the proceeds are expected to be on-lent to blue assets, a relatively new asset class in Brazil. As Santander builds a track record in this segment, other banks are expected to replicate its efforts and catalyze a broader shift in lending practices, embedding resilience and sustainability into their mainstream credit portfolios.

The proposed investment consists of a senior unsecured A Loan of up to US$150 million and a B Loan of up to US$150 million to Banco Santander (Brasil) S.A. (Santander Brasil or the Bank), an existing IFC client since 2009. The proposed investment aims to complement the Banks lending to sustainable projects, with a focus on (i) assets eligible under the Brazilian Governments Eco Invest Program (Eco Invest) and (ii) blue assets, supporting the blue economy. Other sustainable asset categories are also expected to be eligible under the facility such as hybrid and electric vehicles for individuals, sustainable agribusiness practices, and solar panels for individuals (and potentially small and medium enterprises for self-consumption).
